name: litebox
description: A security-focused library OS supporting kernel- and user-mode execution
readmeExcerpt:
# LiteBox

> A security-focused library OS

> [!NOTE]  
> This project is currently actively evolving and improving. While we are
> working toward a stable release, some APIs and interfaces may change as the
> design continues to mature. You are welcome to explore and experiment, but if
> you need long-term stability, it may be best to wait for a stable release, or
> be prepared to adapt to updates along the way.

LiteBox is a sandboxing library OS that drastically cuts down the interface to the host, thereby reducing attack surface.  It focuses on easy interop of various "North" shims and "South" platforms.  LiteBox is designed for usage in both kernel and non-kernel scenarios.

LiteBox exposes a Rust-y [`nix`](https://docs.rs/nix)/[`rustix`](https://docs.rs/rustix)-inspired "North" interface when it is provided a `Platform` interface at its "South".  These interfaces allow for a wide variety of use-cases, easily allowing for connection between any of the North--South pairs.

Example use cases include:
- Running unmodified Linux programs on Windows
- Sandboxing Linux applications on Linux
- Run programs on top of SEV SNP
- Running OP-TEE programs on Linux
- Running on LVBS



## Contributing

aiSummary.oneLiner: A security-focused sandboxing library OS designed to drastically reduce host attack surface.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: LiteBox is an advanced sandboxing library operating system that minimizes the interface to the host, thereby significantly reducing the potential attack surface. It is designed for secure execution in both kernel-mode and non-kernel user-mode environments. The system's architecture focuses heavily on the seamless interoperability between 'North' shims and 'South' platforms, exposing a Rust-inspired, nix-like interface to applications. This highly flexible design allows for incredibly diverse use cases, such as running unmodified Linux binaries on Windows hosts or strictly sandboxing applications on Linux within confidential computing environments.
keyFeatures: Reduced attack surface: Drastically cuts down the exposed interface to the host operating system to improve overall security posture.
Flexible execution modes: Built from the ground up to support deployment in both kernel-mode and non-kernel user-mode scenarios.
Cross-platform interoperability: Facilitates seamless connections between 'North' application shims and 'South' execution platforms.
Rust-inspired interface: Exposes a modern, safe interface inspired by nix and rustix for robust application interaction.
Confidential computing support: Enables running programs securely on top of trusted execution environments like AMD SEV-SNP or OP-TEE.

useCases.title: Cross-platform execution
useCases.description: Developers utilize the library OS to safely run unmodified Linux applications directly on a Windows host environment.

useCases.title: Strict application sandboxing
useCases.description: Security engineers strictly isolate untrusted Linux applications within a highly restricted Linux environment to prevent exploitation.

useCases.title: Confidential computing
useCases.description: Enterprises run highly sensitive workloads securely on hardware-backed environments like AMD SEV-SNP using the LiteBox abstraction.

useCases.title: Trusted execution environments
useCases.description: Systems developers execute specialized OP-TEE programs securely on standard Linux distributions without exposing host interfaces.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: LiteBox is built for systems engineers, security researchers, and developers working on sandboxing, confidential computing, and cross-platform execution. It requires a strong understanding of operating system internals and rust-based system interfaces.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Please refer to the CONTRIBUTING.md file in the repository for detailed setup instructions.
